title: Head & neck cancer: principles
sub: From cause to follow-up: stage by TNM 9, decide at the MDT, then resect and rebuild or irradiate, and watch for late effects.

cards.why: Carcinogens bathe the whole mucosa, so altered fields surround a cancer and give rise to new ones.
see: smoked or smokeless tobacco, betel quid + areca
do: panendoscopy at diagnosis
help to stop smoking · follow for life

cards.why: E6 degrades p53 and E7 inactivates Rb, so p16 is over-expressed.
see: HPV+: younger non-smokers, tonsil, tongue base
cards.warn: Smoking > 10 pack-years worsens the HPV+ outlook.

cards.why: Cumulative sun drives BCC and SCC; blistering childhood sunburn drives melanoma.
do: no shave biopsy of a pigmented lesion
suspected melanoma: excision biopsy, ~2 mm
palpate parotid, neck nodes · test V, VII
cards.warn: Wide excision before diagnosis ruins sentinel mapping.

cards.why: Tissue, extent and a search for second primaries, before the decision.
see: biopsy + FNA · p16 oropharynx · EBV nasopharynx
MRI soft tissue · CT bone, larynx
teeth at risk out before RT

cards.why: Every patient is discussed; the patient's priorities (cure, voice, swallowing, appearance, time) are central.
do: I–II: surgery or radiotherapy alone
III–IV: combined treatment
T4b: chemoradiotherapy or palliation
N0 neck: treat if occult risk > 15–20%
crossing the midline: treat both necks
surgery: clear margin ≥ 5 mm · < 5 mm close

cards.why: BCC destroys locally but almost never spreads; cutaneous SCC can reach the parotid and track along nerves.
see: BCC high risk: H zone, ≥ 10 mm elsewhere, morphoeic
cSCC high risk: ≥ 2 cm, > 2 mm deep, PNI
do: low-risk BCC: 4 mm · high-risk, H zone: Mohs
cSCC: 4–6 mm · high risk 6–10 mm or Mohs
melanoma: 1 cm up to 1 mm thick · 2 cm beyond 2 mm
SLNB if > 0.8 mm (T1b+) · Merkel: 1–2 cm + SLNB
cards.warn: Facial numbness or weakness = perineural spread. No radiotherapy in Gorlin.

cards.why: Cisplatin sensitises the tumour to radiation. Hypoxic cells are two to three times more resistant, and gaps let the tumour repopulate.
see: 70 Gy in 35 fractions over 7 weeks: gross tumour
concurrent chemo: ~6.5% survival gain at five years
do: cisplatin 100 mg/m² three-weekly or 40 mg/m² weekly
audiogram, renal function first
cetuximab only if cisplatin-unfit
haemoglobin to ~12 g/dL · stop smoking
cards.warn: Repopulation speeds up after about four weeks: avoid gaps.

cards.why: Most recurrences come in the first two years, and second primaries keep coming.
see: every 1–3 months in year 1 · 2–4 in year 2
TSH every 6–12 months after neck RT

cards.why: Most are reactive. Cancer here is lymphoma, sarcoma, a neural or thyroid tumour.
see: node > ~2 cm or not shrunk by ~6 weeks
do: ultrasound first
chest X-ray before anaesthesia
whole node, fresh, not formalin
FNA rarely enough for lymphoma
cards.warn: Mediastinal mass: airway can collapse at induction.

cards.why: T is mostly size, but depth of invasion counts in the mouth; N adds extranodal extension.
see: UICC TNM 9 from 1 January 2026 · AJCC v9 aligned
oral T1: ≤ 2 cm and DOI ≤ 5 mm
do: HPV-independent: unequivocal imaging ENE → cN3b
HPV+ oropharynx: ENE moves N up one
nasopharynx: M1a ≤ three · M1b > three
cards.warn: Say which edition: older texts stage differently.

cards.why: Ask what is missing and what it did; use the simplest method that restores function and form.
see: or the elevator: straight to the best
do: irradiated or infected bed: vascularised tissue
no skin graft on bare bone or irradiated bed

cards.why: Most failures come within 48 to 72 hours, usually venous.
see: radial forearm: thin, tongue · Allen test
do: purple, swollen = venous · pale, cool = arterial
either: urgent return to theatre

cards.why: The specimen decides: risk features bring radiotherapy; positive margins or ENE bring cisplatin too.
see: close (< 5 mm) or positive margin · ENE
do: start four to six weeks after surgery
surgery → end of RT < about 11 weeks
60 Gy in 30 · 66 Gy in 33 if close, ENE
positive margin or ENE → + cisplatin

cards.why: Treated in a paediatric oncology centre, under protocols.
cards.warn: Bleeding aural polyp in a toddler: rhabdomyosarcoma until proved otherwise.

cards.why: Permanent; they depend on dose per fraction and total dose.
do: ORN: exposed bone > three months, no tumour
risk > 60 Gy · extract ≥ two weeks before RT
ORN: biopsy · PENTOCLO · fibula flap

text: Zones follow the patient left to right, cause to life after.
Blue: surgical road. Orange: organ preservation.

q.q: cN0 oral tongue cancer, depth of invasion 6 mm.
Resected oral SCC: margin 3 mm, ENE in a node.

abbr.AEIOU: asymptomatic, expanding rapidly, immunosuppressed, older than 50, UV-exposed site
